research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 scoring change
team-level defensive effect as a persistent trait versus regression to the mean
counter strategy (BEST/AVOID) tiers and their link to defensive outcomes
play-type labels derived from play-by-play and their validity
methodological_questions: Is the team-level defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons (year-over-year or split-season reliability) when estimated from raw scoring rather than derived play-type labels?
How much of the H2 suppression signal is regression to the mean, and does a reliability estimate survive RTM and opponent-quality adjustment?
What sample size (team-seasons, possessions, games) is needed to detect a reliability coefficient of plausible size with 120 team-seasons?

historical_evidence.finding: H1 play-type usage as a predictor of H2 suppression: matched ATT for PNR did not survive BH correction (ATT +0.0313, BH_p 0.0658, WEAK; others NULL). Predictive lift over mean reversion was small (0.550 vs 0.511). Record states the bulk of H2 suppression is RTM. Sample n=8873 team-games.

Play-type label backfill verification returned FAIL: PNR 28.7% (band 20-28%), PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, team identity FAIL, 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated. Final verdict FAIL over 921,514 possessions.

Inferred defensive scheme-change labels: within-game change 61.0%, cross-game change 67.7%, transition matrices near-uniform. Record's own caveat: the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform matrices are consistent with label noise.

AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 (inflated n, team-quality confound); series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 with n=50, underpowered (about 80 series needed for p<0.05). Record's observed_verdict is 'inconclusive'; its auto_outcome_status is 'untestable'. Record notes team-quality confounding remains.

A1 adaptation falsification: apparent adapter PPP lift did not hold under asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests (next-game PPP Welch p=0.842). Record classifies the apparent effect as a construction, selection or labelling artifact.

Defensive PPP allowed and opponent possession share, RS vs playoffs, 25 teams: DRIVE allowed 1.191 to 0.923; PNR share +12.1pp, which the record says may reflect tagging differences. Descriptive only, no inferential test.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap in H2 initiator possessions: mean gap +0.427 PPP (n>=10 per tier), same direction as team-level gap. Only 3 players clear n>=30 in both tiers. Concerns player-initiator gaps, not team-level reliability.

Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games (55 series, 25 teams): team AVOID% ranges 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC). Descriptive; player samples 10 to 178 possessions; mechanism unclear per record.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring defensive scheme change from inferred labels
failed_approaches.why: Inferred labels cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution; near-uniform transitions and 99% change rates are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating an apparent adapter PPP lift as a real defensive coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Lift reversed or vanished under asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests; recorded as a construction, selection or labelling artifact, with regression-to-the-mean limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: H1 usage as a predictor of H2 suppression beyond mean reversion
failed_approaches.why: Matched effect did not survive multiple-testing correction; predictive lift over RTM baseline was only +0.039. Record attributes most H2 suppression to RTM.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share as a predictor of winning independent of team quality
failed_approaches.why: Series n=50 underpowered (p=0.07) and team-quality confounded; game-level significance was inflated by non-independent observations.

BEST/AVOID tiers are derived from outcome-linked counter engine output; tier-based definitions could be circular with the outcome.

design.estimand: Year-over-year (and split-season) reliability of each team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 points change, net of an RTM-matched baseline and opponent quality. Report the correlation with a confidence interval, not a yes/no trait claim.
design.unit: Team-season defensive effect (30 teams x 4 seasons; 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons only, complete games).
design.sample: 120 team-seasons, about 90 consecutive-season pairs; playoffs excluded from the primary test; 2025-26 included only once the regular season is complete (from 2026-04-13).
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable reliability (e.g., r about 0.3) and report achieved power by simulation under the observed H2-H1 variance. If power is below 0.8, report the result as inconclusive rather than as a null.
design.controls: Use raw points allowed and possessions (no derived play-type labels). Subtract an RTM-matched baseline (expected H2-H1 change given H1 level and opponent quality). Adjust for opponent strength, pace, and roster or lineup change by season. Use a shuffled-team-label placebo and an H1-only placebo.
design.falsification: The trait claim is rejected if the adjusted reliability CI includes zero, or if the reliability falls to the shuffled-label placebo distribution. The claim is also rejected if the effect disappears after RTM adjustment.
design.multiplicity: One primary reliability test; all secondary cuts (play types, BEST/AVOID tiers, playoff splits) are exploratory and corrected with Holm or BH, labelled as such.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a trait claim only if the adjusted year-over-year reliability is positive with a CI excluding zero, exceeds the placebo distribution, and survives RTM and opponent-quality adjustment. Otherwise report as rejected (if powered) or inconclusive (if underpowered).
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, as of 2026-10-06; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; play-type labels excluded from the primary analysis because of the FAIL verdict in SF-APPA-030.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
